title: HLS Live stream targetDurationUs is not always a ideal way to calculate time for next playlist load
body:
### [REQUIRED] Content description
This issue is related to https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/issues/4217

I also have some content that result in the main issue described here https://github.com/google/ExoPlayer/issues/4217#issue-320953832 

> The issue i'm seeing is when I'm on a good connection, I often get into a very short buffering states (around a second) after playing the stream for a few seconds.

stead of just hardcode the value for **targetDurationUs** as is described there I did this:
https://github.com/fgl27/ExoPlayer/commit/8f298bb23fc7fc061702dd853187ef4d86dfcb9f

But simply setting targetDurationUs to 1s also fix the issue and doesn't seems to add any other, but may cause unnecessary playlist loads.

Including the infromation from https://tools.ietf.org/html/draft-pantos-http-live-streaming-23#page-21
#EXT-X-TARGETDURATION says that all Media Segments will be less or equal to defined value.

this means that we can't restrict the load of a new playlist base on this value (or we can but a furter code check needs to be done to prevent the issue)
as we may have very big #EXT-X-TARGETDURATION = 10 and a small TS size #EXTINF = 1

**this issue usually happens at the beginning of a new playback, after the player has be playing for 30+ seconds all is fine and this doesn't occurs anymore for some time**

I know my change is probably not ideal as is a live stream only issue and if the value of the lowest **#EXTINF** will be used, there is probably a better way to get the value, as if this was supposed to be used on a m3u8 list that is very long will take a lot of time to get the proper value, and the issue may be easier to fix in somewhere else.

I assume if I get this issue others will also get and a proper fix must be done, took me a long time to find that old issue and figure out that I had the same problem.

### [REQUIRED] Link to test content

The content is live and can only be accessed on that moment the link was created, any link shared here will expire or not work as the stream went offline, but I do have the info from the m3u8 files

	#EXT-X-TARGETDURATION:6
	#EXTINF:4.166,live
	#EXTINF:2.000,live
	#EXTINF:1.084,live

### [REQUIRED] Version of ExoPlayer being used
2.10.4

### [REQUIRED] Device(s) and version(s) of Android being used
TV devices running Android 8+

### [REQUIRED] A full bug report captured from the device
Not really device specific issue or something related to logs. This devices that I have don't realy provide usable logs.
